research_question: Does an exposure-homogeneous signed root-polynomial explicit operator generalize from Sony FX3 scene-linear values to the author-prepared Ektachrome scan code domain across held illuminants and held exposure settings, or is root-polynomial regression useful only in the inverse film-correction direction?

epistemic_contract.primary_direction: Sony S-Log3 decoded scene-linear reflection -> author-prepared Ektachrome scan code values
epistemic_contract.inverse_diagnostic_direction: author-prepared Ektachrome scan code values -> Sony S-Log3 decoded scene-linear reflection
epistemic_contract.source_decode: published Sony full-range S-Log3 formula already frozen in src.eval.filmmatch_chart_pairs.slog3_to_linear_reflection
epistemic_contract.negative_scene_linear_values: retained; signed roots are used for mixed monomials and pure powers beyond degree one are deduplicated
epistemic_contract.allowed_claim: development-only paired code-domain explicit-operator capacity evidence for this one author-prepared capture-and-scan source

selection.primary_score: sum of mean held-group RGB RMSE across both outer protocols

decision_branches.forward_capacity_fails: close root-polynomial forward look route under this paired source
decision_branches.inverse_only_passes: record direction asymmetry; treat root-polynomial as correction evidence, not a film-look operator
decision_branches.forward_capacity_passes_but_render_gate_: open only a separately preregistered bounded residual execution challenger
decision_branches.forward_capacity_and_render_gate_pass: open fit-forbidden validation and severe-artifact audit; do not promote automatically

claim_ceiling: development-only directionality and grouped-capacity evidence for deterministic polynomial explicit operators on one author-prepared Sony FX3/Ektachrome E100 paired chart source
